subject: Two or more select inputs with mutual exclusion

messages.author: 129e07bdb789652f
messages.subject: Two or more select inputs with mutual exclusion
parts:
This app generates two select inputs with mutual exclusion : 

 - whenever the user selects the same value as the one in the other selector, this switches the two values 
 - moreover, a subset of a dataframe is created and rendered according to the two selected columns, in such a way that the subdataframe never has two identical columns

code: https://gist.github.com/stla/9033053

run from url: devtools::source_url("https://gist.github.com/stla/9033053/raw/9c3ad4ce296397b923c88b40c2d43e4fbea8e4be/ShinyColumnsSelector.R")

I'd like to know your thoughts about :

 1) Easier solution ?
 2) How to do it for an arbitrary number of select inputs ? 
 3) How to do it more user friendly (for the programmer) ?

messages.author: e718c48d06f126f8
messages.subject: Re: Two or more select inputs with mutual exclusion
parts:
It works.

I had something perhaps a little similar (but perhaps not?) based on ! and %in%, where the user selects a column named input$inputName and the app removes that column from subsequent choices  (the app is big so I'm only posting a snippet):


  output$outputCols <- renderUI({
    if (is.null(input$dataset) || !nzchar(input$dataset)){return(invisible())}
    if (ncol(Data()$df)< 2){return(invisible())}
    # 'drop' = FALSE prevents conversion to vector if data has only one column
    selectInput(
      'inputId' = "inputCols"
      , 'label' = "select column data:"
      , 'choices' = names(Data()$df[,!(names(Data()$df) %in% input$inputName),'drop'=FALSE])     # remove inputName from choice
      , 'selected' = names(Data()$df[,!(names(Data()$df) %in% input$inputName),'drop'=FALSE])[ncol(Data()$df)-1] # pick a column in list
      , 'multiple' = TRUE
    )
  })

messages.author: e718c48d06f126f8
messages.subject: Re: Two or more select inputs with mutual exclusion
parts:
Ah it's perhaps not as easy I first thought.

Can you modify the code below to suit your purpose? Removing the "isolate"s will send the app into an infinite loop. Keeping one isolate and commenting out the other gives almost what I think you want, though not exactly.

Not sure if the symmetrical situation can be done with the right dosage of isolate. 

# ui.R unchanged except the counter removed

# server.R

df <- mtcars

shinyServer(
  function(input, output, session) {
selectx <- reactive({
      isolate(  
          selectx <- selectInput("x", "x", 
          'choices' = names(df[, !(names(df) %in% input$y), 'drop' = FALSE]), # remove input$x from choice
          'selected' = names(df[, !(names(df) %in% input$y), 'drop' = FALSE])
          )
      )
    })

selecty <- reactive({
      #isolate(
          selecty <- selectInput("y", "y", 
          'choices' = names(df[, !(names(df) %in% input$x), 'drop' = FALSE]), # remove input$y from choice
          'selected' = names(df[, !(names(df) %in% input$x), 'drop' = FALSE])[ncol(df)-1]
      #    )
      )
    })
    output$dyncolumns <- renderUI({
        list(selectx(), selecty())
    })
    
    output$subset <- renderTable({
        head(subset(df, 'select' = c(input$x, input$y)))
      } 
      , 'include.rownames' = TRUE
      , 'include.colnames' = TRUE
      , 'sanitize.text.function' = function(x){x}
    )
    
  }
)
